name: FirmaDB API
description:
Use this when you need authoritative company records (legal name, status, address, NACE
classification, registered date, dissolution date, employee count where collected) for
one of 18 European countries. Does direct lookups by national registry id, fuzzy and
structured search, and synchronous batch enrichment of up to 100 (country, registry_id)
pairs in a single call. Does NOT replace sanctions screening, credit bureaus, beneficial
ownership registers, or filings retrieval — FirmaDB exposes registry-derived facts only.

Coverage: ~25.1 million entities served (as of 2026-07-21; see /v1/countries for live figures) across FR, GB, SE, BE, SK, CZ, NO, PL, IE, BG,
LT, FI, EE, RS, CY, CH, LV, SI. Every record carries a `source_url` (where the registry publishes one) pointing to the
underlying government registry page and a `data_freshness` block explaining when it was
last loaded.

Dual audience from day one: human developers (compliance teams, fintech, sales tools)
and AI agents (MCP clients, function-calling, autonomous workflows). Every operation
description in this document follows the same pattern so an agent with zero prior
context can correctly select and call it on the first attempt:
"Use this when [context]. Does [specific action]. Does NOT [common confusion].
Parameters: [example with realistic values]."

Errors are RFC 9457 Problem Details with recovery extensions (`code`, `correction`,
`suggested_request`, `retryable`, `retry_after_seconds`) so agents can self-correct
without re-prompting a human. Every POST accepts an `Idempotency-Key` so retries are
safe. See the Error responses on each operation for the exhaustive code catalog.

Authentication is HTTP bearer with API keys formatted
`fdb_{kid}_{secret}_{check}`. A small set of read-only endpoints
(`GET /countries`, `GET /countries/{code}`, `GET /health`) are available anonymously
with per-IP rate limits.
